existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: ClaimResponse has multiple local hard breaks: required `patient` became required `subject`, adjudication non-money values became `Quantity`, added-item body sites were remodeled, and process-note type changed representation. The top R6-to-R4 uncertainty is how to preserve new R6 optional content and richer datatypes without official cross-version maps.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: The migration themes are path renaming, object-shape replacement, richer datatypes, relaxed R6 cardinalities, and additive R6-only content. R4-to-R6 migration needs deterministic transforms for recipient, adjudication, body-site, and process-note fields. R6-to-R4 migration needs explicit loss policies or extensions for Group subjects, Quantity units, BodyStructure references, optional R6 additions, and records omitting R4-required elements.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural and cardinality findings because both StructureDefinition snapshots were available and matched at the same canonical resource identity. Confidence is medium for terminology nuance because local ValueSet/CodeSystem files were inspected but no live terminology expansion, official diff, or ConceptMap was available.

compatibilityLeverage.note: Resource-level leverage is a planning signal. It does not mark individual Revisit findings as justified or unimportant.

rationaleMd:
ClaimResponse keeps its resource identity. The aggregate has 4 hard R4-to-R6 instance break(s), 1 potential hard break(s), 3 non-mechanical migration finding(s), and 0 direct behavior/API finding(s).

R4 maturity context is trial-use/FMM 2, which creates neutral stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 56/100, producing migration shape `moderate-targeted-remodel`, major migration `Partial`, and compatibility posture `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration`.

6 finding(s) identify a yes/partial less-breaking base-design alternative, so the aggregate should not be used to dismiss local avoidability review.

11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior finding(s) are listed as context but not scored for this resource to avoid duplicating base behavior issues across all resources.
recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Expect targeted migration work, but continue reviewing individual breaks. Use less-breaking designs where they do not preserve obsolete or conflicting models indefinitely.

topFindings.title: Mandatory ClaimResponse.patient was replaced by mandatory ClaimResponse.subject and the target domain widened to Group
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: the R4 `patient` property is not the R6 path and required `subject` is absent; additionally, R6 Group subjects create R6-to-R4 loss.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: ClaimResponse.addItem body-site data was remodeled from flat CodeableConcept fields to repeated backbone entries
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 flat bodySite/subSite properties do not match the R6 nested backbone shape; R6 multiple site groups or BodyStructure references create R6-to-R4 loss.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Adjudication non-monetary value changed from decimal `value` to `Quantity` `quantity`
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 `value` is no longer the R6 property or type; R6 Quantity also creates R6-to-R4 loss when units, system, code, comparator, or extensions matter.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: ClaimResponse.processNote.type changed from primitive code to CodeableConcept
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 scalar code is not the R6 CodeableConcept object; R6 CodeableConcepts without a single recognized R4 code can cause R6-to-R4 loss.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: ClaimResponse.processNote.language binding strengthened from preferred common languages to required all BCP-47 languages
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: local or non-BCP-47 language codings tolerated under a preferred binding may fail the R6 required binding; omitted language remains compatible.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Several R4-required ClaimResponse elements are optional in R6, creating R6-to-R4 validity gaps
topFindings.affectedPath: ClaimResponse.insurer; ClaimResponse.item.adjudication; ClaimResponse.addItem.productOrService; related addItem/detail adjudication paths
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6 can omit elements that R4 requires, and converters cannot safely invent payer, adjudication, or product/service codes without business rules.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.
